coordinatorAmendmentsReceivedMidLane: Second-derivation column is FOUR states, not three, and independently derived means from different SOURCES, not different fields. Test: could one party acting alone produce values satisfying both sides?
The gate is FOUR questions. The fourth is: what bypasses this control?
Question three now reads: what fails when violated, AND is the thing that fails running in production today?
Fail closed applies to OUTPUTS; tooling fails LOUD. A CI check needs a distinguishable third outcome, did-not-run, recorded loudly.
Degradation is permitted only when declared in the output.
Narrow scoping is doctrine: a control whose scope is broader than its claim is a defect, and worse than a narrow one.
Enumerate call sites before scoring a default or check as remediable.

theBuiltArtifact.shape: STRIPPED with a typed refusal. Tier2Overlay.flood is the literal type null; a sibling floodDisposition carries the refusal and its basis.
theBuiltArtifact.whyThereAndNotAtTheResponse: loadBakedNodeFacetSnapshot feeds THREE consumers, not the one the dispatch named. Cutting at the route res.json would have satisfied the dispatch sentence and left the PAID R1 brief serving the identical wrong determination.
theBuiltArtifact.replacementGuardMechanism: Branch on the facet's self-declared provenance.adapterKey, by EXACT equality against a closed const producer set, in a switch whose default assigns to `const unhandled: never`. Adding a producer to the set without adding its case fails tsc.
theBuiltArtifact.whyThatIsNotAnotherPresenceGuard: The input is an identity (which instrument authored this value) rather than a shape (does a key exist and is it an object). It is exact equality, never substring containment. And it is total: recognised producer, unrecognised producer, absent provenance, missing facet and malformed row all resolve to a refusal, so there is no input for which a value is emitted.
theBuiltArtifact.twoIndependentMechanisms: The runtime switch AND the compile-time null type. Either alone would be a single point of failure; the type holds even if the switch were edited away, and the switch holds for producers the type cannot see.

defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.defect: The CI grep was a DEAD GATE: permanently red on a clean tree.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.cause: The comment-strip regex was anchored on ':LINE:', correct for the directory-scanning greps elsewhere in this workflow, but rg given a SINGLE FILE argument omits the filename and prints 'LINE:content'. Nothing was stripped, so the route's own header documentation matched the gate the header describes.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.howCaught: Running the gate against a CLEAN tree and expecting exit 0. A gate observed only failing has not been seen working either.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.fix: rg --with-filename pins the output format; the regex tolerates both forms; POSIX classes replace \s, which is a GNU grep extension.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.significance: This is the exact failure mode ci-coverage-clamp-shared-engine in this same workflow already records in its header. I reproduced a documented defect while implementing the doctrine against it.

defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.defect: The 'cannot pass on its own absence' guard was SENTINEL-SATISFIABLE.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.cause: A single probe for `flood:\s*null` was satisfied by the Tier2Overlay TYPE FIELD alone. Deleting the object-literal assignment in extractTier2Overlay read as clean.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.howCaught: Scenario C of the observation matrix: delete the assignment, leave the type, expect a violation, observed a pass.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.fix: Two markers required and checked SEPARATELY: `flood: null;` (the type floor) and `flood: null,` (the assignment).

defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.defect: The compliant-file self-test fixture did not match the predicate.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.cause: The permitted-assignment pattern is END-ANCHORED, so `flood: null` must sit on its own line. The fixture inlined it as `{ flood: null, floodDisposition: ... }` and was flagged.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.howCaught: Self-test B, which exists precisely to catch a predicate that flags everything.
defectsFoundInMyOwnGateBeforeShipping.resolution: The fixture now mirrors the real formatting, and the constraint is documented rather than removed. Un-anchoring the pattern would swallow `flood: null, legacy: p.flood`, smuggling a value past the gate on the tail of a compliant head.

contradictsTheBriefing.briefingClaim: What currently keeps this off Smart Site is hauska-map apps/property-explorer/src/lib/baked-facets.ts:430, base.includes("/property-atoms"), a substring test deciding which of two semantically different flood answers a caller receives.
contradictsTheBriefing.finding: FALSE as stated, verified at hauska-map d3510a6. Line 430 is not a guard against the flood determination and is not what keeps it off PE.
evidence: PE_FACETS_PROXY_BASE is the compile-time constant "/api/spine/property-atoms" (apps/property-explorer/src/lib/config.ts:22). All five production call sites pass it. The includes() test therefore always takes the property-atoms branch and the else-branch is dead for every shipped caller, so it never selects between two flood answers at runtime.
The /api/spine/property-atoms BFF ITSELF calls cortex GET /api/brokerage/v1/place/node/:id/facets (apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/pe-property-atoms.ts, fetchCortexFacets).

stripCortexEnvelopeProductTruth (same file, ~:175-203) spreads tier2 and nulls ONLY envelope, so tier2.flood is explicitly PRESERVED, and it feeds two response paths that return the cortex body with HTTP 200: the flag-off path (PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH != "1") and the definitive-empty / adapt-failed path.
What actually drops tier2 is mergeBakedBaseFacts in api/_lib/atom-chain-to-facets.ts, which copies only bakedBody.facets and never tier2 — and only on the atom.ok path.
contradictsTheBriefing.theRealGuard: PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH === "1" (an environment variable) AND atomChainIsUsable(chain) for that specific parcel. Both are runtime and data conditions with no test, not a code guard. That is WORSE than the briefing states: an env flip or an unwarmed parcel reopens the path.
contradictsTheBriefing.liveProbeStatus: Code path VERIFIED by reading. Live instance NOT observed. Probed 13 nodes on property-explorer-xi.vercel.app; all 8 that carried a cortex tier2 row also had a usable atom chain, so PE took the atom-chain path and dropped tier2. Per doctrine this is UNMEASURED, not absent, and it is not reported as safe.
contradictsTheBriefing.worseFinding: PE has LIVE consumers of tier2.flood beyond the inspect card, and two read the anonymous cortex route as their documented contract: apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/pe-share-brief.ts:140 `data: tier2?.flood ?? null` builds the ANONYMOUS share view's Flood section, and apps/property-explorer/src/workbench/tools/compare-facts.ts:201 floodCell(tier2) renders a flood cell in the Compare tool, its own header noting it deliberately keeps 'the tier2 sibling the chat path drops'.
contradictsTheBriefing.consequenceForThePlacementOfTheCut: This makes cutting at cortex the ONLY single-point fix. A hauska-map-side fix would have to be replicated across at least four consumers in two repos, each able to regress independently. Retiring at the producer closes all of them at once.

secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.observation: The anonymous route returns floodZone AO with inSpecialFloodHazardArea true for 48021:36521.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.adoptedMechanism: The tier2 bake answered for a tile centre up to 366 m away.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.alternativeMechanism: FEMA NFHL genuinely maps that parcel as AO and the determination is correct for this node.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.whyRejected: The mechanism claim does not rest on this one node being wrong. It rests on the WRITE PATH: fetchFemaTiles queries tileCenter(key), never the parcel centroid, and no predicate tests containment. Under that code, a correct answer for any given parcel is coincidence — the tile happened to be homogeneous. SS-W11's adjudication (0 of 5,714) is the population-level confirmation, and code reading outranks output measuring precisely because sampling outputs applies the same predicate that admitted the defect.

secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.observation: PE production never returned tier2.flood across 13 probes.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.adoptedMechanism: Every probed node had a usable atom chain, so the BFF took the atom.ok path where mergeBakedBaseFacts drops tier2.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.alternativeMechanism: Something downstream strips tier2 unconditionally, so the leak path is unreachable and the finding is moot.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.whyRejected: Read at source: stripCortexEnvelopeProductTruth explicitly preserves tier2.flood and is what the two non-atom paths return. No unconditional strip exists. The negative probes are therefore consistent with 'the atom chain was warm for every node I could find', not with 'the path is closed'. Reported as unmeasured rather than absent.

secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.observation: The CI gate printed 'clean' after I deleted the flood: null assignment.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.adoptedMechanism: The presence probe was satisfied by the type-field occurrence, a sentinel.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.alternativeMechanism: The deletion was not actually applied to the file on disk.
secondMechanismsConsideredAndRejected.whyRejected: The same edit, in the same scenario block, produced the expected tsc failure and the expected vitest failures in adjacent runs, and the offender list printed the surrounding lines. The file was modified; the probe was weak.

residualRisksAccepted: An out-of-repo consumer branching on tier2 truthiness alone will render an empty flood section rather than hiding it. Cosmetic, in the direction of honesty, and no consumer in this repo does it.

hauska-map pe-share-brief.ts and compare-facts.ts will show an EMPTY flood section rather than the refusal once this deploys, because they read tier2.flood and do not know about floodDisposition. That collapses 'refused' into 'absent' on those two surfaces. Declared as leave_behind with a named owner rather than silently accepted; pe-share-brief.ts's own header names cortex buildR1Brief as its contract source of truth, so the drift is already documented as a maintenance obligation there.
The Tier-2 bake keeps writing wrong rows. Deliberate: the rows are SS-W11's evidence and retirement sequences consumers-first. Declared as leave_behind.
